result.report:
PASS for the exact stated partial theorem, using the declared real scalar extension on finite rational spatial domains. This does not complete the original arbitrary-balanced-space classification.

I independently checked the supporting arguments rather than using predecessor verdicts, diagnostics, hashes, or compilation results. The dependency chain is self-contained. I also matched the source packet against the identifiers, formulas, and proof boundaries in the authentic [BMPS v1 PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08664v1), dated March 10, 2026. Its literal coefficient restrictions are explicitly distinguished from the extension proved and used here. No general source continuity, intersection, regularization, or envelope theorem is needed.

The fixed-complex cone lemma is valid, including its claimed broader finite-complex scope. Active constraints correctly characterize tangent cones at every real relative-interior centre, retaining face tangents and lineality. Rational balanced vector-family generators give necessary inequalities through genuine rational-endpoint PCCs. Conversely, those inequalities establish convexity on every contained segment; grouping initial endpoint displacements then proves Jensen for PCCs on arbitrary permitted structures, including remote endpoints. This establishes actual PC, rather than feasibility on one subdivision.

The reference decomposition is exact. The active inequalities define a rational minimal-face subspace containing γ in its relative interior. A sufficiently small rational-coordinate box stays inside that face and satisfies every strict recession inequality. Its vertices are rational-coefficient actual-PC references, each with positive growth, and its positive barycentric weights reproduce γ globally. The construction therefore uses neither approximation nor cone generators that lose growth.

The intersection reconstruction is sufficient in dimension two. The refinement cases preserve inherited balancing and divisor coefficients. In each saturated plane, the quotient-normal representative s/χ gives formula (6); summing its coefficients proves first-divisor balancing. Formula (M) establishes mixed commutativity with every ray and index retained. The rational-centre PCC argument proves PC-to-PAPC against arbitrary nonnegative real local cycles on every ordinary open, in both positive dimensions available here. Consequently both recursive divisors are legitimate, nonnegative cycles. The explicit sequence P+1/n proves decreasing uniform regularizability and has exactly the same PA measures.

The graph geometry reductions preserve the stipulated scope. The positive relation cone forces the entire direction kernel to be one-dimensional. Actual edge weights on each connected component are a positive real scalar times rational weights, with cycle consistency supplied by the existing weights. Every unbranched component is a complete affine line; branching excludes opposite direction pairs. These facts justify the cylinder coface analysis without discarding bounded edges, cycles, ends, full lines, or disconnected components.

The cylinder proof handles arbitrary nonseparable data. Partial fibre infima preserve rational graph PCCs, and finiteness propagates throughout a connected graph. The compact slope interval D exactly controls vertical recession. Fibre vertices supply the finite affine-minimum formulas, while concavity of those formulas makes bounded-edge chords and tail lines valid. The incidence system retains every cycle edge and has a greatest feasible assignment. Rational variable coefficients survive elimination despite real constants, producing rational slope gradients. The common slope supremum then dominates every raw competitor on rational points; enclosing rational simplices extend this domination to every real centre without assuming raw continuity. Applying it to γ−||u||∞ proves both raw envelope equality and two-sided growth.

The rational-domain argument is also valid. Supergradient intervals have rational endpoints, and the normal cones have rational generators, even when slope-chamber endpoints are real. Formulas (21)–(22) therefore give finite rational maximization domains that glue along complete junction fibres. Their vertices lie over graph nodes, so open edge fibres, rectangle interiors, and distant tails hide no additional atoms. At a noncontact atom, a singleton exposed slope set gives zero second divisor. For a nondegenerate exposed interval, strict cap slack forces zero incidence sum; positive weights then force every outgoing slope function to be affine. The resulting germ (27), after affine subtraction, has first divisor supported where the residual function vanishes. Its complete second divisor is therefore zero. This proves full contact in the unbranched case.

For two branched factors, each rational-reference localization is globally controlled by the derived coercivity estimate. Positive sums preserve actual PC and use a common rational refinement without introducing real comparison walls. They reproduce the prescribed real reference outside a compact set and have the common germ C+εH at the selected original junction. The diagonal PCC (36) is genuine on the original product structure and forces the raw junction value. Bounds at all other rational vertices, together with the same-cell vertex/recession argument (38), prove global raw envelope equality using only upper growth. This includes every component, cycle, and end.

The complete saturated junction computation checks out. The kink primitive vector and both indices in (41)–(42) are correct. The tangential corrections give the axis weights in (45); kink weights remain present but contribute zero to the second divisor because H vanishes on those rays. Each axis family contributes 4ab, yielding 8ab with no factorial division. The common local real coefficient therefore gives mass 8ε²ab. The gap is exactly −b₀, equal to −1 at the selected junction and zero at every other original measure vertex. Vertices introduced by the obstacle refinement have zero inherited second coefficient. Hence the complete integral, including all lower-face and refinement contributions, is exactly −8ε²ab<0.

No substantive repair or mathematical wording correction is required. The conclusion is precisely the asserted two-graph fixed-real-reference partial theorem; the other stated residual scopes remain unclaimed.
